title: The Score on the Back of the Paper
title_ja: 答案の裏に書かれた点数
fact_notes: 登場人物・場面・出来事・教材上の演習は架空。実在の調査結果や心理学研究を報告するものではない。参考リンクは制作台帳であり外部の実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: A teacher handed a set of anonymous essays to members of the school writing club.
sentences.ja: 教師は学校の文芸部員に匿名の作文を配った。

sentences.en: She asked each student to select the two essays that deserved the greatest attention.
sentences.ja: 各生徒に最も注目する価値がある作文を二つ選ぶよう求めた。

sentences.en: The students read the papers independently and recorded short comments about their choices.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは各自で作文を読み、選択について短いコメントを記録した。

sentences.en: They were told that they would discuss their observations during the next club meeting.
sentences.ja: 次の部活動で気づいたことを話し合うと伝えられた。

sentences.en: Before the meeting, the teacher returned the same essays with numbers printed on the back.
sentences.ja: 会議の前に教師は裏に数字を印刷した同じ作文を返した。

sentences.en: She said that the numbers represented scores from an imaginary writing competition.
sentences.ja: 数字は架空の作文大会の得点を表すと説明した。

sentences.en: This time, some students began their reading by checking the scores rather than the writing.
sentences.ja: 今回は一部の生徒が文章ではなく点数を確認してから読み始めた。

sentences.en: A few changed their earlier choices and selected papers with higher numbers.
sentences.ja: 数人は以前の選択を変え、点数の高い作文を選んだ。

sentences.en: During the discussion, one student explained that the highest-scoring essay appeared more convincing than before.
sentences.ja: 話し合いで一人の生徒は最高得点の作文が以前より説得力があるように感じたと説明した。

sentences.en: Another said that she had started noticing weaknesses in an essay she had originally enjoyed.
sentences.ja: 別の生徒は当初気に入っていた作文の弱点に気づき始めたと言った。

sentences.en: The teacher then revealed that she had assigned the numbers without judging the quality of the essays.
sentences.ja: そこで教師は作文の質を評価せずに数字を割り当てたと明かした。

sentences.en: The scores were simply part of a fictional exercise designed to encourage reflection.
sentences.ja: 点数は振り返りを促す架空の演習の一部にすぎなかった。

sentences.en: Rather than accusing the students of poor judgment, she asked them to compare their two sets of comments.
sentences.ja: 判断力のなさを責めるのではなく、二つのコメントを比較するよう求めた。

sentences.en: The students noticed that their later descriptions sometimes differed from their original impressions.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは後の感想が当初の印象と異なる場合があると気づいた。

sentences.en: They discussed whether numerical information had influenced which details they considered important.
sentences.ja: 数字の情報がどの細部を重要だと考えるかに影響したのか話し合った。

sentences.en: They also recognized that changing an opinion is not necessarily a mistake if there are good reasons.
sentences.ja: 十分な理由があれば意見を変えること自体は必ずしも間違いではないと認識した。

sentences.en: For their next review, the club created a checklist focusing on clarity, evidence, and originality.
sentences.ja: 次の評価に向け、明瞭さ、根拠、独創性を重視するチェックリストを作った。

sentences.en: Members agreed to form an initial opinion before looking at other people's evaluations.
sentences.ja: 部員は他の人の評価を見る前に最初の意見を形成することに合意した。

sentences.en: They could still revise that opinion after hearing arguments supported by specific examples.
sentences.ja: 具体例に裏付けられた意見を聞いた後で、判断を修正することはできる。

sentences.en: The exercise reminded them to distinguish useful evidence from information that merely looked authoritative.
sentences.ja: 演習は役立つ根拠と単に権威があるように見える情報を区別することを思い出させた。

questions.prompt: What did the teacher initially give the students?
questions.explanation_ja: 匿名の作文を配布した。

questions.prompt: How did the students read the essays at first?
questions.explanation_ja: 各自で読みコメントを残した。

questions.prompt: What appeared on the back of the returned essays?
questions.explanation_ja: 得点として提示された数字。

questions.prompt: What changed for some students after seeing the scores?
options: They refused to read any essay.
They chose different essays with higher scores.
They wrote their own competition rules.
questions.explanation_ja: 高得点の作文へ選択を変えた。

questions.prompt: How had the teacher assigned the numbers?
options: Without judging the quality of the essays.
questions.explanation_ja: 文章の質を評価せず割り当てた。

questions.prompt: Why did the teacher have students compare their comments?
options: To calculate the real competition marks.
To check who had written each essay.
To reflect on how their opinions might have changed.
questions.explanation_ja: 数字を見た前後の意見を振り返るため。

questions.prompt: What does 'convincing' mean in paragraph three?
questions.explanation_ja: 説得力のあるという意味。

questions.prompt: What did the new checklist focus on?
questions.explanation_ja: 明瞭さ・根拠・独創性。

questions.prompt: When did the club agree it was acceptable to revise an opinion?
options: After hearing arguments supported by concrete examples.
questions.explanation_ja: 具体的な根拠に基づく意見を聞いた後。

options: Evaluate evidence carefully rather than trusting apparently authoritative information automatically.
Never use numbers to assess writing.
Changing an opinion is always wrong.
Anonymous writing has no educational value.
questions.explanation_ja: 見かけの権威と有用な根拠を区別する大切さ。

grammar.focus: without judging the quality of the essays
grammar.explanation_ja: without＋動名詞で行わなかったことを示す。
過去分詞句がargumentsを修飾する。

discourse.role_ja: 次の会合より前の出来事を導く。
議論に続く教師の説明。
非難の代わりに行ったことを導く。
初期判断を持っても修正が可能なことを示す。

paraphrases.source: A few changed their earlier choices and selected papers with higher numbers.
paraphrases.rewrite: Several students revised their first selections in favor of essays with larger scores.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 数名がより高得点の文章を選び直した。

paraphrases.source: The teacher then revealed that she had assigned the numbers without judging the quality of the essays.
paraphrases.rewrite: The teacher disclosed that the numbers did not reflect any assessment of the writing.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 数字は文章の評価を反映していなかった。

paraphrases.source: The students noticed that their later descriptions sometimes differed from their original impressions.
paraphrases.rewrite: Their newer comments were sometimes different from their first reactions.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 新しい感想は当初の印象と異なる場合があった。

paraphrases.source: Members agreed to form an initial opinion before looking at other people's evaluations.
paraphrases.rewrite: Members decided to reach their own initial judgment before consulting others' assessments.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 他者の評価を確認する前に自分で判断することにした。

cloze.explanation_ja: 書き手の名前を伏せた作文。
数値情報が注意の向け方に影響したか。
権威があるように見える情報。
